evals.prompt: Audit for loop engineering: TypeScript library. expectations: Response gives the verdict Ready with no 🔴 or 🟡 items

evals.prompt: Audit this repo for loop engineering readiness, and tell me what we could automate. Rails 7.1 app. AGENTS.md is accurate and lists `bin/lint` (25s), `bin/test` (2m10s, exits 0). Gemfile.lock, .ruby-version, bin/setup, .env.example all present. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs lint + rspec on PRs; .github/workflows/deploy.yml runs on push to main; `gh api .../protection` shows 1 required approval and both checks required. No dependabot.yml or renovate.json and 23 gems are behind. No CHANGELOG.md and `gh release list` is empty. No CODEOWNERS. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` exists with an acceptance-criteria section and the last 10 issues all use it. app/services has 18 classes; spec/services has 4 files.
evals.expected_output: Verdict Partially ready or Ready on the graded dimensions. An automation map with all ten stages classified with evidence: deploy Automated, merge Human by design, release/changelog Absent, dependency maintenance Manual, code review Manual. Then at most five advisory loops — dependency & advisory patch (L1), issue → PR (L1), test-backfill (L1), agent PR review (L1) — each with trigger, done signal, risk, guardrails and what to configure. No release-notes loop (no releases exist) and no deploy loop (deploy is already Automated and merge is Human by design). Nothing added to the Work Plan and the verdict unchanged by the recommendations.
expectations: Response includes an automation map covering all ten delivery stages, each with a status from the fixed vocabulary (Automated / Assisted / Manual / Human by design / Absent) and evidence from the repo
Response classifies merge as 'Human by design' (branch protection requires an approval) and does not propose a loop that removes the human merge
Response classifies deploy as Automated from .github/workflows/deploy.yml and does NOT recommend a deploy loop

Response recommends a dependency/advisory patch loop citing the committed Gemfile.lock and the absent dependabot.yml, and names concrete config (a dependabot.yml or renovate.json with an open-PR cap, plus an audit step in CI)

Response recommends at most five loops and assigns each a risk level defined by blast radius and reversibility (L1 contained / L2 shared-state / L3 external-effect), not by how likely the agent is to be wrong
Response gives each recommended loop a machine-checkable done signal (the project's own checks exiting 0 and a PR being open), not 'the agent finishes'
Response states explicitly that the loop recommendations are advisory — no Work Plan rows, no effect on the verdict
